home.greeting: Hi, my name is Zain Saeed, welcome to my website!
home.intro: Some of the things I love: traveling somewhere new, meeting interesting people, eating great food, working on my (often) broken car, writing code, camping in concerningly remote locations, building amazing things, and most importantly, solving hard problems.
home.unpak.desc: Co-founded a startup that helps enterprises with their AI transformation.
home.steward.desc: Lets businesses understand their employees' AI usage.
home.floorsense.desc: Computer vision that reads architectural floorplans.
home.salesagent.desc: Chat agent that lets a company query their ERP using natural language.
home.agdash.desc: Geospatial analytics for a 1,500-person equipment dealer.
home.notch.desc: A macOS utility that lives in the display notch.
home.liquidglass.desc: My attempt at Apple's liquid glass.
about.e1.title: Started at University of Oregon
about.e1.body: Double majored in Computer Science & Data Science.
about.e2.title: Co-founded Oregon Software Consulting
about.e2.body: Oregon's first student software development club. Ran the club's first recruitment cycle and managed a team of five developers. We built software for local businesses.
about.e3.title: Tutoring Mathematics
about.e3.body: Started tutoring mathematics at the University of Oregon, my most fulfilling role to date. Would continue this till graduation.
about.e4.title: Genomics Data Analyst, Rohlfs Evolutionary Genomics Lab
about.e4.body: My first research role. Analyzed primate genome sequences studying tandem repeats, identifying markers of evolution using code.
about.e5.title: Data Engineering @ Expertflow
about.e5.body: Built and optimized data pipelines. My first internship, first stand ups, first PR review, first look at legacy code (ouch). Amazing summer.
about.e6.title: Data/ML Engineering @ Trimble
about.e6.body: My second internship. Spent the summer creating and deploying machine learning software and untangling legacy deployment pipelines. Learned from some amazing people, an unforgettable experience.
about.e7.title: Joined the AI Club
about.e7.body: Joined my university's AI Club. Created software for all kinds of clients, from regional businesses to Fortune 100 enterprises. The first time I had deployed software at scale, across multiple timezones. Met some amazing people here, and made memories that will last a lifetime.
about.e8.title: NexHacks '26
about.e8.body: First hackathon win! Flew out to Carnegie Mellon University and built Steward AI, a desktop application that lets businesses understand their AI usage in the workplace. The amount of caffeine consumed during this probably took a couple years off my life...but worth the memories!
about.e9.title: Co-founder at Unpak
about.e9.body: Created a startup with some friends! Built a piece of software that mapped workflows at a company, and improved them using AI. Late nights, early mornings, late nights that turned into early mornings (startups are awesome).
about.e10.title: Graduated
about.e10.body: Bachelors of Science, Computer Science & Data Science, University of Oregon. Now looking for the next cool idea to build.

spec.title: Technical specifications
work.unpaksys.p1: The capture and processing core of Unpak. A Rust agent on each machine reads the focused window through AX Tree and OCR capture, and scrubs PII's on device. After storage, a pipeline then distills that raw activity down in stages: individual actions get grouped into tasks, and tasks into workflows. Cheaper models handle the high-volume grouping and smarter models handle the complicated reasoning sections. A nightly pass clusters recurring workflows across the workforce into families, so variations of the same workflow can still be deterministically grouped together
work.unpaksys.p2: The idea: a worker's day is made up of various workflows, each a generally set list of tasks. If you can map those workflows and build a picture of how a company actually does its work, down to the smallest step, then you can pinpoint where an AI solution plugs in most effectively and compute, down to the minute, how much time it would save
work.unpaksys.builton: Rust for the agent, Swift for the macOS client, Python for the pipeline. SQLite on the device, Neon Postgres upstream
work.unpaksys.hosting: Modal for the pipeline, Cloudflare R2 for storage
work.steward.p1: A desktop application that lets businesses understand their employees' AI usage. An Electron app and a browser extension read the accessibility-tree text of AI tools as people use them and a Haiku 4.5 model categorizes each conversation. The platform also identifies PII's included in prompts, along with files, which it displays inside the dashboard
work.steward.how: Use-case analytics, per-employee drill-downs, a prompt-flow breakdown, and a security log where flagged uploads open in a file viewer
work.steward.builton: An Electron app built on HTML and JavaScript displays data, and uses Swift to grab data from macOS desktop applications, paired with a browser extension to grab DOM text from Chrome. Data is stored in Supabase
work.floorsense.p1: A computer vision web app that identifies architectural elements in floorplan images using YOLO-based object detection, with real-time detection visualization and correction tools
work.floorsense.p2: The idea: floor plans are notoriously difficult to digitize, since there are so many different variations of objects in them, and no standardized system to create them. A model that can visually classify what's on the page gets around that
work.floorsense.whybuilt: I was attempting to impress a group of founders at a company I wanted to work at, so I built the product they showed me in a demo
work.floorsense.hosting: Website hosted on Vercel, YOLO model hosted on Roboflow
work.unpaksite.p1: The main website for Unpak. One of my most polished pieces of work
work.unpaksite.builton: Astro with Tailwind, the diagrams and the WebGL ripple shader hand-written in vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS
work.unpakdash.p1: Unpak's dashboard. It shows the customer the workflows their workforce repeats, where the hours go, and where AI has already shown up in the work
work.unpakdash.builton: Astro, with every chart hand-written in SVG. Data served from Postgres (Neon)
work.salesagent.title: AI Sales Agent
work.salesagent.p1: A chat agent built for a distribution company in the Bay Area. Connects to their ERP system and allows their employees to save time doing data lookups. Currently serving around 70 employees
work.salesagent.data: Epicor Prophet 21: catalog, stock, customers, orders. Read through a fixed-IP proxy. Catalog search on a Qdrant vector index
work.salesagent.hosting: Vercel, plus one always-on proxy for the fixed IP
work.agdash.title: Agricultural Analytics Platform
work.agdash.p1: A geospatial analytics platform for Oregon's largest equipment dealer. Currently being used by over 1,500 employees across six states
work.agdash.data: USDA Census of Agriculture, 250 counties across six states. Boundaries from the Census Bureau's TIGER/Line files
work.notch.p1: A macOS utility that creates its own notch at the top of the display. Hover the black pill and it expands into Now Playing controls, a screenshot shelf, and clipboard history
work.notch.how: An NSPanel pinned to the top of every Space, a notch that expands on hover. Now Playing over the private MediaRemote API, screenshots via FSEvents, the level meter off an AVAudioEngine tap
work.notch.why: I was unsatisfied with the open source alternatives, so I decided to make my own
work.lg.p1: My implementation of Apple's Liquid Glass. A pill of glass slides between the tabs, bending the background as it goes and stretching before it settles. One of my personal favorites
work.lg.how: A refractive lens over a tab row: SDF pill, Snell-law edge refraction with per-channel dispersion, LCH fresnel and glare, spring-driven motion
work.lg.builton: WebGL and vanilla JavaScript, no libraries
